messages:
Connor O'Brien: release coordination for Optimize guardrails gating (feature flags + rollout stages + CS/Support comms). trying to land a concrete plan by EOD so we can prep next week’s train.

Connor O'Brien: current plan draft:
- `optimize.guardrails_gating_mode` = `observe_only` -> `soft_block` -> `hard_block`
- `optimize.guardrails_override_enabled` (RBAC-gated)
- per-tenant allowlist for pilot

Connor O'Brien: questions:
1) when do we flip observe_only in prod? (so we start collecting pass/fail + latency)
2) who owns comms to CS/Support + what’s the exact customer-facing behavior for “timeout”?
3) do we ship release notes at soft_block or hard_block?

Aditya Rao: +1. also need a crisp “what changed” blurb for CS. last time we did Optimize behavior change we got a bunch of “why did my apply fail” tickets.

Sean Gallagher: from SRE POV: observe_only in prod ASAP is fine, but we should do it behind traffic shaping so eval runner load doesn’t spike.

Sean Gallagher: i’d propose:
- Day 0: observe_only prod for internal tenants only (Redwood + dogfood) for 24h
- Day 1: expand observe_only to 5% tenants (random) + all pilots
- Day 3: 25% tenants
- Day 5: 100% tenants

Sean Gallagher: then soft_block only for pilot allowlist until we hit SLOs (eval p95 + backlog stable).

Marissa Cole: product wants to avoid “soft_block everywhere” until the override path + messaging are solid. but agree with observe_only broad to find weirdness.

Paula Mendes: reminder that “soft_block” still means support load. even if override exists, customers will ping us. we should time soft_block to business hours and have oncall + CS briefed.

Owen Phillips: on CS side: if we’re turning on observe_only, that’s invisible to customers right?

Jordan Lee: observe_only is “evaluate + log + audit event emitted” but apply proceeds. no UI surface unless we decide to show “quality checks ran” somewhere. (currently console hides it)

Kenji Nakamura: UX note: we *do* show a small “Quality checks” badge in the apply details view once the eval run completes, even in observe_only. it’s not blocking, but it’s visible.

Owen Phillips: ok then we need enablement docs bc support will get “what is this badge” questions.

Dylan Brooks: console team can add a tooltip copy for observe_only: “Checks are informational; this change was not blocked.” but we need final wording from PM/legal-ish.

Naomi Feldman: for comms: make sure we don’t imply we guarantee “no regressions” or that the eval suite represents their entire workload. wording should be “helps prevent” + “based on configured prompt sets/suites.”

Miguel Santos: pilots: Acme Fintech is expecting hard blocks (they asked explicitly after last incident). Northbridge probably wants soft blocks first. we should segment.

Aditya Rao: +1. can we do:
- pilot tier A: hard_block + override
- pilot tier B: soft_block + override
then GA: soft_block default first, hard_block after 2 weeks?

Sean Gallagher: i’m nervous about hard_block pilot before we’ve proven runner reliability. if runner hiccups, you just blocked their ability to apply optimizations entirely.

Sean Gallagher: unless we do safe-degrade rule: on runner outage, enterprise tier goes to “manual approval required” vs full block.

Jordan Lee: policy engine supports mode switching on dependency health, but we need to align on default:
- if runner down: (a) block all, (b) allow with risk banner, (c) require override justification.
right now PR is (c) for enterprise, (a) for self-serve.

Paula Mendes: (c) is the only one i can live with for hard_block pilots. and we should rate limit overrides.

Connor O'Brien: ok, summarizing a proposal for release train:

Connor O'Brien: Phase 1 (next train):
- prod: observe_only on for 100% tenants by end of week (ramped: 0%->5%->25%->100%)
- pilot allowlist: soft_block only (no hard_block yet)
- override path enabled only for internal + pilot (RBAC)

Connor O'Brien: Phase 2 (following train, contingent on SLOs):
- pilot allowlist: hard_block for “tier A” design partners who request it
- start GA with soft_block for enterprise only

Connor O'Brien: Phase 3:
- default-on hard_block (all tiers) after 2 weeks of soft_block + low false positive rate

Marissa Cole: that’s close. for Phase 2 GA: we probably want soft_block for “Dedicated/Private” first, then hosted self-serve last.

Aditya Rao: agree. hosted self-serve is where messaging matters the most and prompt sets are weakest.

Owen Phillips: what do we want Support to tell customers during soft_block?

Aditya Rao: draft:
- “Optimize ran quality checks on your configured prompt sets / standard suites.”
- “It detected a regression in X metric (link).”
- “You can rerun (if flaky) or request an override (if permitted) with justification.”
- “If you don’t have prompt sets, we used Redwood standard suites tagged to your route type.”

Naomi Feldman: please add: “Overrides are audited.” and remove anything implying “standard suites cover your production traffic.”

Dylan Brooks: also need consistent naming: in UI it’s “Quality guardrails”, not “gating”. Support macros should match.

Miguel Santos: can we include a simple table for CS:
- status: PASS -> applied
- status: FAIL -> blocked (soft) + override option
- status: TIMEOUT -> try again; if urgent, request override
- status: ERROR -> treat like timeout

Sean Gallagher: TIMEOUT needs an SRE playbook link for CS: “check status page? check incident channel? if ongoing, tell customer we’re investigating.”

Connor O'Brien: action items:
- Aditya + Naomi: finalize customer-facing wording for PASS/FAIL/TIMEOUT (EOD tomorrow)
- Owen: draft CS macro + internal enablement doc (by Friday)
- Sean: ramp schedule + alert thresholds for observe_only rollout (by Friday)
- Dylan/Kenji: tooltip copy for observe_only badge (by next Tuesday)

ReleaseBot: (auto) Release train cut: next production deploy window is 2025-01-07 10:00–12:00 PT. Freeze begins 2025-01-06 17:00 PT.

Paula Mendes: for release notes: i’d do a short internal-only note at observe_only, and customer-facing notes at soft_block GA (Phase 2). hard_block can be a follow-up note.

Marissa Cole: +1. if we put customer-facing notes at observe_only we’ll just create questions without any behavior change.

Aditya Rao: ok. we’ll do customer-facing “what’s new” when it can block or require action.

Jordan Lee: FYI: if we’re doing 0->5->25->100 observe_only, we should confirm metric cardinality labels are safe at 100%. (we’re adding `prompt_set_rev` and `suite_id` tags)

Sean Gallagher: good catch. we’ll sample suite-level labels at 10% and keep aggregate counters at 100%. i’ll note in rollout doc.

Connor O'Brien: perfect. i’ll post the finalized release plan in eng-releases channel once Aditya/Naomi confirm wording + Owen confirms support enablement timeline.

Owen Phillips: works for me. i’ll also ping support leadership so they don’t get surprised when “Quality guardrails” starts showing up in screenshots.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: once you finalize, tag me and i’ll make sure console copy lands in the same train (or we hide badge until copy is ready).

Kenji Nakamura: i’d prefer not hiding the badge (it helps build trust) but ok to gate behind `optimize.guardrails_badge_enabled` if needed.

Connor O'Brien: let’s keep badge enabled for internal, and flip for external tenants when copy is approved. (feature flag: `optimize.guardrails_badge_enabled`).

Paula Mendes: +1, and align with CS enablement date.

Sean Gallagher: ok. i’ll make sure the rollout checklist includes badge flag sequencing too.
